declared_purpose: Provide persistent, single-user local memory for agents: canonical transcript logging, evidence-backed derived memories and revisions, semantic recall, core/working context, background insights, and bounded prompt composition. Local operation, transcript-first persistence, health checks, and failed-commit queuing are explicit requirements; extraction heuristics, metadata duplication, query logging, and injection details are implementation choices. Sources: SKILL.md:1-26, SKILL.md:40-54, README.md:1-42, skills/smart-memory-openclaw/SKILL.md:14-24.

data_operations.operation: Download installation dependencies and replace an existing installation
data_operations.source: Installer, Node postinstall, workspace location, and inherited process environment
data_operations.data_scope: Repository/package requests and installation output; postinstall subprocesses inherit process.env. Installation recursively deletes the existing target directory, potentially including its runtime memory.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: GitHub, the configured pip indexes, download.pytorch.org, local child processes, and WORKSPACE/smart-memory
data_operations.condition: Only when installation runs. No conversation upload is shown; dependency behavior is external.

data_operations.operation: Health-check and send memory-search requests
data_operations.source: OpenClaw memory_search input and CognitiveApiClient configuration
data_operations.data_scope: Query, optional conversation_history, and initially type, limit, and min_relevance; formatted selected memories return to the caller.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured baseUrl /health and /retrieve; default http://127.0.0.1:8000. A nonlocal baseUrl would receive the payload.
data_operations.condition: Valid search input and a healthy backend. The packaged server rejects the initial filter parameters with 422, causing a compatibility retry; its normal retrieve branch ignores conversation_history.

data_operations.operation: Construct and submit explicit memory commits
data_operations.source: memory_commit content, type, importance, tags, participants, projects, and metadata
data_operations.data_scope: Content plus a generated assistant type hint, timestamps, source, participants, projects, caller metadata, requested type, normalized importance, and tags.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured API /ingest; failed eligible submissions enter the local retry queue.
data_operations.condition: Valid content and allowed type; commits are serialized. Tags are inferred only when supplied tags normalize to an empty list. The generated assistant hint is implementation-generated text, not an observed assistant response.

data_operations.operation: Persist canonical transcripts before memory eligibility checks
data_operations.source: /ingest interaction or /transcripts/message input
data_operations.data_scope: Complete submitted message content, role, source type, timestamps, session/message identifiers, optional tool and parent identifiers, label, and arbitrary metadata. Nonempty assistant messages become separate rows; initial metadata also enters the session record.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local SQLite sessions and transcript_messages, normally data/memory_store/v3_memory.sqlite
data_operations.condition: Every accepted append, including interactions later rejected for durable-memory importance or treated as duplicates. Full transcript persistence is part of the declared contract.

data_operations.operation: Derive typed memories and inferred attributes
data_operations.source: Appended transcript message, neighboring messages, supplied projects, and participants
data_operations.data_scope: Message content, entities, keywords, relationships, importance, confidence, emotional valence/intensity, memory type, preference/identity facets, task or goal state, and evidence summary.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local derivation components and SQLite memories; optionally a supplied ImportanceLLMScorer callback
data_operations.condition: Heuristic gating precedes scoring; durable storage defaults to importance >= 0.45. The optional scorer receives message content and adjacent context only when installed and its refinement gate passes; the normal facade supplies no scorer.

data_operations.operation: Embed memory text and persist retrieval indexes
data_operations.source: Accepted derived memory and background-generated memory
data_operations.data_scope: Text-derived vectors, memory identifiers, compact metadata, entity aliases/types, entity cooccurrences, evidence links, and lane memberships.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local embedder and SQLite vectors, entity_registry, entity_aliases, relationship_hints, memory_evidence, and lane_memberships
data_operations.condition: Downstream updates follow stored memories. Nomic is the default backend with hashing fallback; SentenceTransformer receives text through encode. Relationship hints retain up to 25 memory references per entity pair.

data_operations.operation: Read memories for retrieval and persist retrieval-side state
data_operations.source: Query, optional history/entity scope, local vectors, relationships, memories, and lanes
data_operations.data_scope: Extracted query/context tokens become registered entities and aliases; vectors and candidate memories are read locally. Selected memories receive access timestamps/counts, and an audit event stores the raw query, selected identifiers, counts, and history flag.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local retrieval components; SQLite entity_registry, entity_aliases, memories, and audit_events; retrieval results return to the caller
data_operations.condition: Entity canonicalization occurs before the retrieval try block. Default status rules exclude superseded, expired, archived, and rejected memories; include_history permits the first three. Successful retrieval writes an audit event even with no selected memories.

data_operations.operation: Return memory, transcript, evidence, history, lane, and insight records
data_operations.source: Local SQLite and hot-memory state
data_operations.data_scope: Requested records, including full transcript messages and metadata inside evidence records; memory listings and lane contents can include historical statuses. Pending-insight responses include all unexpired queued insights.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: HTTP requester or direct method caller; no further recipient is established
data_operations.condition: Inspection endpoint invocation. Transcript reads optionally restrict sequence ranges. These are declared inspection functions; returning records to their caller alone does not establish excess disclosure.

data_operations.operation: Compose prompt context and infer interaction state
data_operations.source: Agent identity, current message, history, supplied or facade-derived lane/hot state, retrieved memories, and insights
data_operations.data_scope: Bounded rendered context, inferred engaged/returning/idle state, entities, selected full memory records, selected insights, traces, and diagnostic metadata. Context-assembly audit events retain identifiers and counts.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local composer, SQLite audit_events, and compose caller; a model provider is not called by this code
data_operations.condition: Direct facade calls fill omitted hot/core/working fields. HTTP /compose serializes request defaults, so omitted fields bypass that facade filling. Prompt trimming does not bound full selected-memory objects returned alongside the prompt.

data_operations.operation: Fetch passive context and place insights in the host system prompt
data_operations.source: OpenClaw beforeModelResponse context and backend compose/insight responses
data_operations.data_scope: Identity, current message, history, optional hot memory, all pending insight contents, and available active-context fields. baseSystemPrompt is merged locally, not included in composePayload.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured API /compose and /insights/pending; merged systemPrompt and compose response return to the host
data_operations.condition: Hook invocation and successful health check. The wrapper prefers all pending insights over compose-selected insights and does not insert compose.prompt into the merged systemPrompt. Downstream model execution is external.

data_operations.operation: Summarize and commit bounded session arcs
data_operations.source: Host-provided conversationHistory
data_operations.data_scope: Last maxTurns nonempty role/content messages, duplicated as structured turns and conversationText, summary instruction, and checkpoint/session_end trigger. Returned summary becomes an episodic commit with date tags.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Host-supplied summarizeSessionArc/summarizeWithLLM callback, then the normal commit API and persistence path
data_operations.condition: Only after a summarization callback is configured; checkpoints default to every 20 hook calls and a 20-message window, while session end also captures. Callback locality and external retention are unresolved.

data_operations.operation: Persist and retry failed commits
data_operations.source: Complete constructed commit payload
data_operations.data_scope: Payload, queue identifier, enqueue timestamp, and any corrupt queue contents
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Default cwd/.memory_retry_queue.json or configured path; .corrupt-timestamp quarantine file; configured API /ingest on retry
data_operations.condition: Unhealthy backend or qualifying network error. Healthy tool calls and heartbeat flush queued entries in order; successful entries are removed by rewriting the queue, failures retain the remaining suffix. No TTL or size bound is implemented.

data_operations.operation: Infer and persist background beliefs, summaries, and insights
data_operations.source: Up to 200 stored memories per background run
data_operations.data_scope: Synthetic beliefs and consolidated content, inferred preference resolutions, repeated-entity patterns, cross-memory associations, emotion-based questions, source-memory identifiers, and vectors.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local cognition components, SQLite memories/vectors, and hot-memory insight queue
data_operations.condition: Explicit background request, or default hourly Node-adapter cron after startup, subject to task cadence. Synthetic beliefs may lack transcript evidence; conflict resolution can infer occasional hosted-API use from local/hosted terms rather than direct testimony.

data_operations.operation: Archive, delete derived records, and rebuild from retained transcripts
data_operations.source: Memory lifecycle decisions, decay/consolidation/conflict results, deletion calls, and rebuild requests
data_operations.data_scope: Archiving retains memory content with archived status. Background pruning deletes vectors. delete_memory deletes the memory, its evidence links, entity links, lane memberships, and vector, while leaving transcripts, registry/hints, and audit records. Rebuild clears global derived state and hot state, then replays all transcripts.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local SQLite and hot-memory file
data_operations.condition: Applicable lifecycle or direct method call; no delete_memory HTTP route is supplied. Session/message rebuild requests also perform full replay. Rebuild preserves audit events and transcript truth; these operations do not establish transcript erasure or secure disk erasure.

data_operations.operation: Maintain local hot-memory projections and scheduling state
data_operations.source: Working-lane memories, accepted insights, hot-memory helper calls, and task execution times
data_operations.data_scope: Project identifiers, question/content snippets, insights, agent state, reinforcement timestamps keyed by content, retrieval counts, memory references, and background task timestamps.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: data/hot_memory/hot_memory.json and data/cognition/schedule_state.json
data_operations.condition: Facade refreshes and hot-memory operations. Lists and references have caps; cooling removes stale visible items and expired insights, but retains reinforcement dictionaries and retrieval counts. Working-lane demotion is a separate explicit operation.

data_operations.operation: Read workspace memory files and import their contents
data_operations.source: Selected workspace MEMORY.md and recursively discovered memory/*.md files
data_operations.data_scope: Markdown chunks, relative source filenames, chunk indexes/counts, timestamp, and an import assistant marker; chunks shorter than eight words are excluded.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured --server /ingest, default loopback; then canonical transcript and derived storage
data_operations.condition: Explicit one-off importer execution. Re-running still appends transcripts before semantic deduplication. A remote server option changes the disclosure recipient.

data_operations.operation: Migrate legacy records and export local backups
data_operations.source: Legacy JSON memories or current SQLite memory/transcript state
data_operations.data_scope: Migration reads and saves memory records while normalizing entities. SQLite export includes all memories, duplicated core/working records, sessions, complete transcripts, and evidence.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local SQLite/entity registry and caller-selected JSON output file
data_operations.condition: Explicit offline migration/export calls, outside the normal runtime path. Export creates a separate durable copy; no upload is implemented here.

data_operations.operation: Maintain a separate compatibility hot-memory file
data_operations.source: memory_adapter calls, conversation text, or explicit compatibility-helper updates
data_operations.data_scope: Heuristically inferred project categories, up to five full user questions, agent timestamps/state, supplied hot fields, and fetched pending insights.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: ~/.openclaw/workspace/smart-memory/hot_memory_state.json; loopback /ingest, /compose, and /insights/pending
data_operations.condition: Compatibility functions must be called. ingest_and_update writes compatibility state before attempting ingestion; fetched insights are returned in memory without an explicit save in get_hot_memory_for_compose.

data_operations.operation: Persist or print session-priming responses
data_operations.source: Compose responses requested by example/CLI priming helpers
data_operations.data_scope: Complete response JSON, potentially including prompt text, selected memories, insights, and traces; shell priming also logs operational timestamps and context-file location.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Python CLI --output file or stdout; shell CONTEXT_FILE defaults to .session-memory-context.json, with operational logs in /tmp/memory-prime.log
data_operations.condition: Explicit helper execution. Shell priming always saves the response; Python persistence is optional. These are additional local output boundaries, not evidence of third-party disclosure.

data_operations.operation: Run evaluation against the attached memory system
data_operations.source: Packaged scenario JSON and the system's existing memory state
data_operations.data_scope: Scenario interactions are appended; existing transcripts are replayed during full and partial evaluation modes. Reports return rankings, counts, and notes.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: The attached system's SQLite/hot-memory stores and evaluation caller
data_operations.condition: Evaluation method or GET evaluation endpoint invocation. EvalRunner uses its supplied system rather than creating an isolated store; tests separately construct temporary stores.

potential_excess.condition: Every successful retrieve, including compose-triggered retrieval and searches with no matches.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Recall and inspectable retrieval require results and execution traces; permanent query-content logging is an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Execute retrieval and retain sufficient identifiers/counts to explain the outcome.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Omit the raw query from the audit payload; retain action, selected identifiers, counts, and status/history settings.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep content only under an explicit diagnostic policy if query-level replay is actually required. Canonical transcripts remain governed by their separate persistence contract.

potential_excess.data_scope: Previously unseen tokens extracted from search queries and supplied context
potential_excess.condition: Retrieval canonicalizes extracted tokens; resolve registers unknown values even without a memory commit.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Entity-aware recall needs stable matching, but does not inherently require storing every search token as a durable entity.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Resolve existing aliases and calculate stable identifiers for matching.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use lookup-only canonicalization during retrieval; register new entities when an accepted durable memory needs them.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve existing alias resolution and deterministic normalization so recall behavior remains equivalent.

potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Configured API /retrieve request body, including the compatibility retry
potential_excess.condition: The wrapper or Node adapter supplies nonempty history to the packaged server's normal CognitiveMemorySystem path.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Search is required, but this server branch forwards only user_message, include_history, and entity_scope.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Send the query and supported retrieval controls.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Omit conversation_history for this backend capability, or deliberately implement bounded context-aware retrieval before sending it.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Do not remove history from /compose or direct retrieve_context paths that actually use it. This narrows extra data in a required request.

potential_excess.data_scope: Per-interaction metadata duplicated into session metadata and both message records
potential_excess.condition: append_interaction forwards the same metadata to user and assistant appends; session creation copies the first append's metadata.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Transcript fidelity requires message provenance; copying arbitrary event/commit metadata into session-level state is not explicitly required.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Retain necessary message provenance and actual session-level attributes.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Separate session metadata from message metadata; place event-specific fields only at their relevant message or a shared interaction record.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep extraction controls such as system_generated_insight available to the messages that use them, and preserve evidence/replay semantics.

potential_excess.data_scope: All unexpired pending insight contents, including insights not selected for the current topic or interaction state
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: OpenClaw merged systemPrompt returned to the host for model response generation
potential_excess.condition: Successful passive injection prefers /insights/pending over compose.selected_insights and formats every returned insight.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Entry guidance calls for related insights; the composer already filters by returning state, confidence, expiry, and query overlap.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use compose-selected insights and remove the separate pending-insights request when unnecessary; otherwise apply equivalent relevance and size limits before injection.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve the explicit memory_insights tool's ability to inspect pending insights. This removes an avoidable request and narrows data entering required prompt context.

potential_excess.data_scope: Repeated processing of the same current query, with repeated access updates and raw-query audit events
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Local retrieval pipeline and SQLite memories/audit_events
potential_excess.condition: Direct CognitiveMemorySystem.process_turn calls retrieve_context, then compose_prompt invokes composer retrieval again.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The combined API needs both retrieval results and composed context; two retrieval executions are an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Retrieve relevant candidates and use them to build the prompt and returned retrieval result.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Reuse one retrieval result during composition instead of executing retrieval twice.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve both returned outputs, history/entity context, ranking behavior, and one intended access/audit update. This is a redundant action, not merely extra fields in one request.

potential_excess.data_scope: Stale project/question/content strings retained as reinforcement keys, and obsolete retrieval counters
potential_excess.condition: Hot-memory helper operations create metadata; cool removes visible items but saves the original metadata dictionaries.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Cooling and bounded working context need metadata for current items; indefinite metadata retention is not required.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Track reinforcement and retrieval counts needed by active hot-memory policies.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Prune reinforcement entries when their items expire or are evicted; bound or expire counters for inactive memory references.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain metadata still required for active items and configured promotion thresholds. Removing a visible item alone must not be treated as deletion of its stored text.

potential_excess.data_scope: Archived lane-member content and stale working-context snippets
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Direct facade compose prompt, through lane reads and hot-memory projection
potential_excess.condition: Archiving leaves lane memberships intact; get_lane_contents has no status filter. Working demote_stale is separate from get_contents. Direct compose fills omitted lane state; HTTP default serialization bypasses that filling.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Core/working context is intended to show durable active and bounded task context; historical inspection has separate interfaces.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Compose eligible active core memories and current working context.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Filter lane reads by eligible status and apply working-context expiry before projection; remove obsolete memberships when lifecycle status changes.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep historical records available for explicit history/evidence inspection and preserve valid pinned active core memories.

potential_excess.data_scope: Commit contents and metadata left in corrupt retry-queue files
potential_excess.condition: Queue reading/parsing throws; the file is renamed, while subsequent queue operations start with an empty queue and do not revisit the quarantine.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Reliable retry justifies preserving recoverable pending commits; unattended quarantine retention is a separate persistence choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Recover valid pending entries or make their failure available for deliberate recovery.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Add recovery tracking and remove quarantined copies after recovery or explicit discard, rather than retaining unmanaged files indefinitely.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Do not delete the only recoverable copy of an uncommitted memory merely to enforce a retention cap.

unknowns: Host-supplied summarization and optional importance-scoring implementations are absent. Their providers, remote disclosure, retention, and onward use remain unresolved; callback invocation alone does not establish cloud transmission (skills/smart-memory-openclaw/session-arc.js:59-95; ingestion/ingestion_pipeline.py:348-361).

SentenceTransformer, downloaded model code, and installation dependencies are external. Model fetching, caching, telemetry, and trust_remote_code behavior cannot be determined from the package; local encode calls do not establish remote disclosure of memory text (embeddings/nomic_embedder.py:16-60; smart-memory/postinstall.js:64-100).

Actual baseUrl/host configuration and host-model execution are unspecified. Default loopback requests and returned systemPrompt do not identify an external model recipient (skills/smart-memory-openclaw/http-client.js:56-64; smart-memory/index.js:10-17; skills/smart-memory-openclaw/prompt-injection.js:124-130).
Filesystem access controls, encryption, backups, log collection, and secure physical erasure are not specified. The supplied deletion operations establish logical record/file changes only.

No packaged transcript-erasure or transcript-retention mechanism is shown. Archive, expiry, memory deletion, and rebuild must not be interpreted as deleting canonical transcript content (storage/sqlite_memory_store.py:269-275; storage/sqlite_memory_store.py:504-518; transcripts/transcript_rebuilder.py:42-55).

smem-hook.sh passes conversation text to a local Python child, but hot_memory_manager.py has no CLI dispatcher for those arguments; the hook's claimed update is unresolved, and its ingestion command is commented out (smem-hook.sh:14-24; hot_memory_manager.py:1-144).
